text:
maria.g: FYI — Hyperscale just signed the enterprise commit (3yr, committed spend). Need quick sizing + security checklist before legal signs. They expect mixed chat+embedding workloads.

alex.k: Congrats. Do we have their traffic profile? QPS, avg tokens, peak burst windows?

maria.g: From presales: baseline ~120 RPS, avg 40 tokens/req, 95th-minute bursts up to 600 RPS for ~10m during marketing events. Latency SLO is p95 < 250ms for chat.

sam.t: For that shape I'd recommend reserved pool + autoscale headroom. Rough math: baseline token throughput = 120 * 40 = 4800 tps. Peak = 600*40 = 24000 tps.

sam.t: If one GPU (our standard infer node) can sustain ~6k tps for chat model-v1 (quantized) with KV caching, then baseline -> 1 reserved, but peak -> ~4 GPUs. Recommend reserved baseline 2 GPUs and autoscale up to 6 to handle bursts + buffer.

alex.k: Can we justify 2 reserved vs 4? Sales asks about cost delta and failure modes.

sam.t: Two reasons: 1) reserved 2 give predictable baseline latency and cheaper committed rate; 2) autoscale to 6 with immediate warm fallback covers burst without permanent reservation. Also preheat window + KV warmup reduces cold overhead.

maria.g: Legal/security wants answers for questionnaire: VPC, KMS, audit logs, SOC2, data residency. Also they asked if Private deployment required for PHI.

lee.ops: For VPC & KMS we can offer Private; Hosted supports customer-managed KMS for keys at-rest and per-tenant audit logs. For PHI we advise Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) or dedicated with encryption & BAA.

alex.k: Sales needs a short runbook and a config snippet for ops to hand to the customer (autoscale policy, reserved min/max, burst credits). Can you paste something simple?

sam.t: Pasting a minimal autoscale example they can use in onboarding:

```yaml
reserved_capacity: 2  # GPUs reserved (baseline)
autoscale:
  min: 2
  max: 6
  scale_policy: latency_based
  target_p95_ms: 200
  cooldown: 120s
burst_credit_pool: 6000  # token-equivalent for short bursts
kv_cache:
  prewarm_minutes: 15
  retention: 24h
```

sam.t: Notes: burst_credit_pool expressed in token-equivalents; adjust based on model size. Prewarm scheduled 15m before expected marketing events.

maria.g: Perfect. Also they asked about overage pricing if autoscale kicks in beyond commit. What should we quote?

lee.ops: Standard: committed discount applies to reserved baseline; autoscale usage billed at on-demand tier with tiered overage caps. We usually offer a capped overage rate for enterprise (e.g., 20% premium over committed unit price) as a negotiation point.

alex.k: Can we include an SLA clause around autoscale latency during burst events? They want p95 during burst as well.

sam.t: SLA can state p95 <= 300ms during allowed bursts if autoscale hits max; otherwise we commit best-effort beyond that and provide fallback to smaller model variant to maintain latency. Need ops sign-off.

maria.g: Ops — can you confirm warmup playbook for KV cache and preheat triggers? Also need a short list for the security questionnaire about KMS key rotation & audit endpoints.

lee.ops: Will sync. TL;DR for questionnaire: KMS (customer-managed ok), HSM option for Private, SOC2 Type II report link, VPC peering support, per-request audit logs retention policy (default 90d, configurable), and endpoint allowlisting.

preheat-bot: Reminder: schedule KV prewarm 15 minutes before any predicted spike. Use `redwood preheat --pool hyperscale --minutes 15`.

maria.g: Great — I'll turn this into a one-pager for the AE and attach the YAML + security bullets. Anything else?

alex.k: Add rollback policy: if autoscale fails, system should route to a smaller but lower-latency model or degrade gracefully (rate-limit non-critical routes). Also capture cost impact numbers for finance.

sam.t: I'll produce a capacity estimate table (reserved vs autoscale vs peak) and an ops checklist by EOD.

maria.g: Thanks team — getting legal to sign depends on the checklist. I'll loop in AE and legal after Sam posts the table. :thumbsup:
